about.title: Welcome to Nazareth Holy Cross
about.description1: Nazareth is at the heart of the Christian faith. Not everyone can travel to Nazareth, the city where Jesus grew up and where spiritual experiences await every visitor, so we are pleased to bring Nazareth to you.
about.description2: Through our website, you can take a virtual tour of the main churches and holy sites of Nazareth, connect to the rich history and religious tradition that characterises the place. In addition, we offer you a unique opportunity to purchase local souvenirs and even light a candle in memory or honor of your loved ones, as if you were here with us.
about.description3: In our online shop you will find crosses of local olive wood, rosaries, jewellery inspired by Christian symbols, stained glass and a keepsake set of water, soil, olive and incense from Nazareth. You can also have a real candle lit for you in a church in Nazareth, and receive a video of it.
about.description4: We invite you to open your hearts and feel the warmth of our community through every product you choose to buy. Every purchase supports the local community and helps preserve the rich heritage of Nazareth for future generations. Visit our website and find your way to connect with Nazareth, anytime and anywhere.

whatIsNew.touchingTheSacred: Touching the sacred, feeling the heartbeat

introParagraphs.part1: Nazareth, the city where the miraculous unfolded, is the place where Jesus took His first steps and grew up in the home of Mary and Joseph. Here, within the ancient churches, at the spring where Mary drew water, and in the vibrant market of the old city, you will find your faith coming to life once more.
introParagraphs.part2: Imagine yourself walking through the narrow streets, following in Jesus’ footsteps to the churches, sharing moments of reflection at Mary’s Well, where the holy mother drew water from the ancient spring. Every stone, every alley, tells a story of unwavering faith, of a spiritual journey that transcends time.
introParagraphs.part3: When you light a candle in the Basilica of the Annunciation, you join your prayer to the place where Mary said yes to God. And when your heart longs for Nazareth, our souvenirs carry something of its holiness, reminding you of your deep connection to the place where it all began.
introParagraphs.part4: Allow us to bring Nazareth to you, straight into your home. With every memento, you preserve a deep bond with Nazareth – the city where Jesus and Mary walked, the city where faith was born. Remember the moments that happened here, the hearts that opened in prayer, and the tears that quietly fell upon the ancient stones.
introParagraphs.part5: Nazareth awaits you, embracing you from afar, bringing its holiness to you. Keep the flame burning in your heart, until the day you return to us – to the city where faith beats.

headerGreek.title: Explore the beauty of the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation

contentGreek.paragraph1: The Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation, also known as St Gabriel’s Church, sits above the spring where Orthodox Christians believe the Annunciation took place. As the Virgin Mary went to draw water from the spring, the Archangel Gabriel appeared and informed her that she would conceive and give birth to a son who she would name Jesus. The current church dates back to 1750, when Daher al-Omar, the ruler of the Galilee, gave the Greek Orthodox community permission to build it.
contentGreek.paragraph2: The church has a central nave with two aisles and contains a beautiful wooden iconostasis donated by a Greek merchant in 1767. The church was redecorated by Romanian artists from 1977 to 1978. An arched passageway leads down to a small chapel, which is decorated with Armenian tiles and has seven steps leading to the spring, believed to have been built by the Crusaders in the 12th century.
contentGreek.paragraph3: About 140 metres from the church is Mary’s Well, which was once fed by the spring and served as a local source of water for several centuries. The fountain was repaired in 1967 and again in 2000 but does not function today.

headerLatin.title: Explore the beauty of the Basilica of the Annunciation

contentLatin.paragraph1: The Basilica of the Annunciation, the Catholic church at the heart of Nazareth, is one of the largest churches in the Middle East and holds deep religious significance for Christians worldwide.

history.title: Historical background
history.text: The site is traditionally believed to be the place where the Angel Gabriel announced to the Virgin Mary that she would conceive and give birth to Jesus, an event known as the Annunciation. The basilica has a long history dating back to the early centuries of Christianity, with successive churches built on the site over time.

architecture.title: Architectural features
architecture.text: The current basilica, built between 1960 and 1969, has a distinctive two-storey structure. The upper church is used for worship services, while the lower church encloses the Grotto of the Annunciation, believed to be the actual site of the Annunciation. The basilica's architecture blends modern styles with traditional elements, and its interior is adorned with mosaics, frescoes, and artworks depicting scenes from the life of Christ.

visiting.title: Visiting the basilica
visiting.text: The Basilica of the Annunciation is a popular destination for pilgrims and tourists visiting Nazareth. Visitors can explore both the upper and lower churches, admire the artistic and architectural features, and participate in religious ceremonies and events held at the basilica. The site offers a profound spiritual experience and serves as a symbol of faith and heritage.

headerMary.title: Explore the beauty of Mary's Well

contentMary.intro: Mary’s Well, also known as the Virgin’s Fountain, is the old well house of Nazareth, fed for centuries by the town’s spring. The spring itself rises about 140 metres away, inside the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation (St Gabriel’s Church), where Orthodox tradition places the Annunciation: there the angel Gabriel first greeted Mary as she came to draw water.

significance.title: Historical and religious significance
significance.biblicalText: The Gospel of Luke tells how the angel Gabriel was sent to Mary in Nazareth. An ancient tradition, kept by the Orthodox Church, adds that the angel first greeted her as she was drawing water at the spring. That is why the spring, and the well it fed, are linked with the Annunciation.
significance.culturalText: The well has been a vital source of water for the local community for centuries. It served as a gathering place for the people of Nazareth, making it an integral part of daily life in the town.
significance.architectureText: The well house was once fed by the spring that rises in the crypt of the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation, about 140 metres away. The church dates back to the 18th century, but the spring and the site have much older roots.

modern.title: The site today
modern.restorationText: The fountain at Mary's Well has undergone several restorations over the years, notably in 1967 and 2000. Despite these efforts, the well does not function today as it once did.
modern.attractionText: Mary’s Well is a popular stop for pilgrims and visitors, who come to see the historic well house and continue to the spring inside the Greek Orthodox church, where by Orthodox tradition the angel first greeted Mary.
modern.surroundingsText: The well is located in Nazareth's Old City, an area rich with historical and religious landmarks. Nearby attractions include the Basilica of the Annunciation, the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation, and various other sites related to the life of Jesus and Mary.

visiting.title: Visiting Mary's Well
visiting.locationText: Mary's Well is situated in the heart of Nazareth, making it easily accessible for visitors exploring the Old City.
visiting.accessibilityText: The site is open to the public and can be visited throughout the year. It is advisable to check local visitor information for any specific visiting hours or guidelines.
visiting.culturalExperienceText: Visiting Mary's Well offers a unique opportunity to connect with the rich religious and cultural heritage of Nazareth. The site provides insight into the daily lives of the people in ancient times and their spiritual practices.

headerTitleNaz: Explore the beauty of the city of Nazareth

contentNaz.introduction: Nazareth’s Old City is best known for its souk, a market of narrow stone lanes where spice sellers, bakers and craftsmen still keep their shops. Around it lie many of the city’s Christian sites, among them the Basilica of the Annunciation, the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation and the Synagogue Church.

historicalSignificance.title: Historical and religious significance
historicalSignificance.text: Nazareth is prominently mentioned in the New Testament. According to Christian tradition, it is the site where the Angel Gabriel announced to Mary that she would bear Jesus, an event commemorated by the Basilica of the Annunciation. Archaeological evidence indicates that Nazareth was a small Jewish village during the time of Jesus. It has been continuously inhabited since antiquity.

modernNazareth.title: Modern Nazareth
modernNazareth.text: The city has a diverse population, predominantly Arab Muslims and Christians. As of recent estimates, Nazareth has around 77,000 residents. Nazareth is a vibrant cultural center with various religious, cultural, and educational institutions. It hosts festivals and events that reflect its rich heritage and diverse community. Tourism is a significant part of Nazareth's economy, driven by its religious sites and historical landmarks. Additionally, the city has a mix of small businesses, shops, and markets contributing to its local economy.

accessibility.title: Accessibility and tourism
accessibility.text: Nazareth is well-connected by road, with frequent bus services from major cities like Tel Aviv, Haifa, and Jerusalem. The city offers various accommodation options, from hotels to guesthouses, catering to the needs of tourists and pilgrims.

meta.title: Visitor guide to Nazareth
meta.description: Everything to prepare your visit to Nazareth: how to get there from Haifa, Tel Aviv and Ben Gurion airport, dress code, best seasons, safety, money and the weather by month.

hero.title: Visit Nazareth
hero.lead: Practical answers for pilgrims and travellers: getting there, what to wear, when to come and what to expect.

getting.title: How to reach Nazareth
getting.lead: Nazareth sits in the hills of Lower Galilee in northern Israel, an easy trip from the coast.

haifa.title: From Haifa
haifa.text: The simplest route: about 40 minutes by car or taxi, or about an hour by bus.

telaviv.title: From Tel Aviv
telaviv.text: About 1½ hours by car, longer at rush hour. Direct buses run from Tel Aviv to Nazareth; you can also take the train to Haifa or Afula and continue by bus.

airport.title: From Ben Gurion Airport
airport.text: About two hours by car or taxi. By public transport, take the train to Haifa or Tel Aviv and continue by bus; a pre-booked shuttle or a rental car is the easiest.

local.title: Once you are in Nazareth
local.text: The holy sites are all within about 15 minutes' walk of each other, so you can park once and explore on foot. Parking in the centre is limited, so arrive early or use a car park at the edge of the old town.

dress.title: Dress code
dress.text: Churches ask visitors to cover shoulders and knees, women and men alike. A light scarf or shawl in your bag solves it. Wear comfortable shoes: the old lanes are steep and uneven.

etiquette.title: Etiquette
etiquette.text: Speak softly in the churches and put your phone on silent. Remove hats inside. Photography is usually allowed, but not during services; ask before photographing people.

seasons.title: Best seasons
seasons.text: Spring (March to May) and autumn (late September to November) are mild and the most pleasant for walking. Summer is hot and dry; winter is cool and rainy. Easter, Christmas and the Feast of the Annunciation (25 March, and 7 April at the Greek Orthodox church) are the busiest and most moving times.

safety.title: Safety
safety.text: Nazareth is generally welcoming and calm, but conditions in the region can change. Check your government's travel advice before you go, follow local news, and keep valuables close in crowds.

money.title: Money
money.text: The currency is the Israeli new shekel (ILS, ₪). Cards are widely accepted and there are ATMs in the centre; carry some cash for market stalls and small cafés. Polite bargaining is part of shopping in the market.

language.title: Language
language.text: People speak Arabic and Hebrew, and in the places pilgrims visit you will find English and often other languages too. A few words of Arabic are always warmly received.

climate.title: Weather by month
climate.lead: Typical conditions in Nazareth: warm, dry summers and cool, wet winters.
climate.caption: Average daily temperatures and rainfall by month
climate.note: Figures are rounded long-term averages, for guidance only. Weather varies from year to year; check the forecast before you travel.

free.q: Are the churches free to enter?
free.a: Entry to the main churches is generally free and donations are welcome. Each church sets its own hours and rules, so check before your visit.

dress.a: Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees, and comfortable shoes for steep lanes. Bring a light layer in winter and sun protection in summer.

days.q: How many days do I need?
days.a: Most pilgrims see the main holy sites in one full day. Two or three days let you slow down for prayer, the Old City market and trips around Galilee.

safe.a: Nazareth is generally calm and welcoming, but conditions in the region can change. Check your government's travel advice and local news before and during your trip.

season.q: When is the best time to visit?
season.a: Spring and autumn are the most comfortable. Summer is hot and winter is rainy. Easter, Christmas and the Annunciation (25 March, and 7 April at the Greek Orthodox church) are the busiest and most moving times.

meta.title: Nazareth in the Gospels
meta.description: Read the Gospel passages about Nazareth, from the Annunciation to Jesus in the synagogue, each with a short reflection and the holy site that keeps its memory alive.

hero.title: Nazareth in the Gospels
hero.lead: Eight passages that name Nazareth, in the order of the story, each paired with the place you can still visit.

intro.title: From the Annunciation to “Come and see”
intro.text: Nazareth appears in the Gospels as the town of the Annunciation and of the hidden years of Jesus. Read a passage, pause over the reflection, then follow the link to the holy site.

gospel.note: Quotations are given for reflection and may differ slightly from the Bible translation you use. Passages: Luke 1, 2 and 4; Matthew 2; John 1.

luke126.quote: In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin pledged to be married to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.
luke126.text: The whole story begins in a small hill town. Walk through Nazareth today and you walk where the Gospel begins.

luke130.text: Beneath the Basilica of the Annunciation lies the grotto that Christians have venerated for centuries as the place of Mary's home, where the angel's greeting is remembered.

luke138.text: Orthodox tradition remembers the angel first speaking to Mary as she went to draw water, at the spring that rises inside the Greek Orthodox Church of the Annunciation. Her answer is the heart of every pilgrim's prayer.

matthew223.text: After the return from Egypt, Joseph settled his family in Nazareth. From then on Jesus was known as “Jesus of Nazareth”, and the name of the town travelled across the world.

luke240.text: Of the hidden years we are told very little: a child growing up in an ordinary town. The lanes and market of the Old City help you imagine that daily life.

luke251.quote: He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother kept all these things in her heart.
luke251.text: For centuries the spring of Nazareth was where the town gathered each day. Standing at Mary's Well, you can picture the ordinary work and quiet faith that Mary kept in her heart.

luke416.quote: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. On the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue, as was his custom, and stood up to read.
luke416.text: Jesus returned to preach in the town where he had grown up. Sites in the Old City, including a church traditionally placed on the site of the synagogue, recall that day.

john146.text: Philip's answer to Nathanael is the invitation of every pilgrimage: Come and see. Nazareth is still best understood by walking its streets.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: What personal data Nazareth Holy Cross keeps when you order, light a candle, share a prayer or write to us, why we keep it, and how to ask us to change or delete it.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: We keep as little as we can. This page explains what we keep, why, and your choices.

who.title: Who we are
who.p1: This website is run by Nazareth Holy Cross, which shares the holy places, prayers and crafts of Nazareth with pilgrims everywhere. For any privacy question, write to {email}.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.p1: We collect only what you give us when you use a service:

items.orders: Orders: your name, e-mail address, phone number, delivery address, the items you bought, the total and the date.
items.candles: Candle requests: your name, e-mail address and your prayer.
items.prayers: The prayer wall: the name, country, category and prayer you write. These are shown publicly.
items.reviews: Reviews: your name, the place you are from and your message, shown on the site once approved.
items.contact: Contact messages: your name, e-mail address, phone number and message.
items.payments: Payments: handled by PayPal. We do not receive or store your card number.

items.u1: To fulfil and deliver your orders, and to light your candle and send you the video.
items.u3: To show prayers and approved reviews on the site, as you intended.

share.title: Who else sees it
share.p1: We do not sell your data. A few services help us run the site and process data on our behalf:

items.paypal: PayPal processes payments under its own privacy policy.
items.hosting: Our website, servers, database and image storage are run by hosting providers, which may store data outside your country.
items.maps: When you open a map or directions, or watch a video from another site, that site's own privacy policy applies.

browser.title: What stays in your browser
browser.p1: The site has no accounts and does not use advertising or analytics cookies. Your browser stores:

items.liked: The prayers you said Amen to, so that you can say it once.

browser.p2: We count how many times some pages are opened and how many payments are completed, per day and per advertising campaign. These are plain totals: they use no cookie and no identifier, store nothing in your browser, hold nothing about you, and are not shared with anyone.

keep.title: How long we keep it
keep.p1: We keep orders and candle requests for as long as we need them to serve you and to meet our legal and accounting duties. Prayers and reviews stay on the site until you ask us to remove them.

rights.title: Your choices
rights.p1: You can ask us to show, correct or delete the data we hold about you, or to remove your prayer or review. Write to {email} and we will respond. Depending on where you live, the law may give you further rights.

children.title: Children
children.p1: The site is not aimed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data. If you think a child has sent us data, write to us and we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: If we change this policy we will update the date at the top of this page.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: Simple rules for using the site, ordering and sharing. By using the site you agree to them.

use.title: Using the site
use.p1: You may use this website for personal, non-commercial purposes. Please do not misuse it, try to break its security or send harmful or unlawful content.

orders.title: Orders and payment
orders.p1: Orders are paid through PayPal. Prices are in US dollars and are calculated by our server when you pay, not by your browser.

items.i1: Every order gets a discount of {discount} on the items and a flat shipping fee of {shipping}.
items.i2: We may cancel an order, with a full refund, if an item is unavailable or a price is clearly wrong.
items.i3: Delivery, customs and returns are explained in Shipping and returns.

candles.title: Candles
candles.p1: A prayer candle costs {price}. We light a real candle for your intention in the church you choose, film it and send the video to your e-mail address within 48 hours of your payment. If the video does not arrive in that time, or something in it is wrong, write to us and we will refund you in full.

donations.title: Donations
donations.p1: Donations are voluntary and support the work of Nazareth Holy Cross. If you donated by mistake, write to us as soon as possible.

content.title: Prayers and reviews
content.p1: When you share a prayer or a review, you tell us it is your own and that you are happy for it to be shown on the site.

items.i1: Do not post hateful, unlawful or misleading content, or other people's personal details.
items.i2: We may remove anything that breaks these rules or that we find inappropriate.

ip.title: Our content
ip.p1: The texts, photos, videos and design of the site belong to Nazareth Holy Cross or to the people who allowed us to use them. Please ask before you copy them for anything other than personal use.

info.title: Information on the site
info.p1: We do our best to keep the site correct, but opening hours, prices and travel conditions can change. Always check locally before you travel.

liability.title: Liability
liability.p1: The site and its services are provided as they are. To the extent the law allows, we are not responsible for losses caused by using the site or by events outside our control. Nothing here limits rights that the law gives you as a consumer.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: We may update these terms. The date at the top of the page shows the latest version.

meta.title: Accessibility statement
meta.description: How accessible Nazareth Holy Cross is: the WCAG 2.2 level we meet, the accessibility settings, known limitations and how to reach our accessibility coordinator.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.lead: We want everyone to be able to use this site, whatever their abilities, device or language.

commitment.title: Our commitment
commitment.p1: Nazareth Holy Cross is made for pilgrims around the world, many of them older or reading on a phone. We want every visitor to be able to light a candle, read about the holy sites, shop and give, with a keyboard, a screen reader, a magnifier or a touch screen.

status.title: Conformance status
status.p1: This website partially conforms to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA, the level that the Israeli Standard IS 5568 also requires. Partial conformance means that the pages we build meet level AA in the checks described below, while some content, listed under known limitations, does not yet.
status.p2: This statement covers the public website nazarethholycross.com in all 14 languages. It was last reviewed on {date}.

settings.title: Accessibility settings
settings.p1: The button with the accessibility sign in the bottom corner of every page opens settings that apply to the whole site and are remembered in this browser. The reset button returns everything to the original look.

items.contrast: High contrast: black background, white text and brighter gold.
items.motion: Stopped animations, moving photos and film. If your device asks for less motion, the site already follows it.
items.font: A readable font: one plain typeface instead of the decorative headings.
items.spacing: More space between lines, letters and words.
items.focus: A strong focus ring that shows where the keyboard is.

items.keyboard: Every page can be used with a keyboard alone, with a visible focus ring and a link that skips to the main content.
items.structure: Every page has one main heading, headings in order, named regions and its language declared, so screen readers can read it correctly.
items.contrast: Text and controls meet the WCAG contrast ratios, and every image has a text alternative or is marked as decorative.
items.zoom: Text can be enlarged to 200 percent, and pages fit a screen 320 pixels wide without scrolling sideways.
items.forms: Forms have visible labels, explain each error in words next to the field and keep what you typed.
items.motion: Moving backgrounds have a pause button, and nothing moves by itself for visitors who ask for less motion.
items.languages: Hebrew and Arabic pages are mirrored from right to left, and buttons and links are large enough to tap.

limits.title: Known limitations
limits.p1: These parts do not yet fully meet level AA. Until they do, write to us and we will help you another way.

items.paypal: Payment: the PayPal buttons and payment window are made by PayPal, and we cannot change them. If you cannot use them, write to us and we will find another way to complete your order or gift.
items.videos: Videos: the recordings of past broadcasts and the films on the tour page do not have captions or transcripts yet.
items.translations: Translations: most texts were translated with the help of software and are waiting for review by native speakers, so some wording may be unclear.
items.external: Other services: the player of our live broadcasts and recordings (Cloudflare Stream, shown in our pages), maps and social networks, whose accessibility we do not control.
items.photos: Photographs: their descriptions name the place and the subject, but do not describe every detail.

testing.title: How we checked
testing.p1: We tested every page in English, Hebrew and Arabic, on a computer screen and a phone screen: automatically with axe-core against the WCAG 2.2 A and AA rules, and by hand with the keyboard, with 200 percent text, at 320 pixels wide and with each accessibility setting switched on.
testing.p2: We have not yet tested with every screen reader, browser and device. If something does not work for you, please tell us.

contact.title: Contact the accessibility coordinator
contact.p1: If you meet a barrier on the site, need information in another format or have a suggestion, write to our accessibility coordinator at <mail>{email}</mail>. Please tell us which page you were on and what you were trying to do.
contact.p2: We read every message and will reply as soon as we can.

calendar.lead: The great feasts of the Catholic and Orthodox Churches. Nazareth keeps both, so where their dates differ you see both.

notes.title: About the dates
notes.catholic: Catholic dates follow the Gregorian calendar, as the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem and the Basilica of the Annunciation keep them. When a solemnity falls in Holy Week or on a Sunday of Lent or Advent, it moves to the day the Roman calendar sets.
notes.holyLand: In the Holy Land some Catholic parishes, in Galilee and elsewhere, keep Easter and the feasts that depend on it on the Orthodox date, and parishes usually keep Corpus Christi on the following Sunday. Ask your parish for its dates.
notes.orthodox: Orthodox dates follow the Julian calendar of the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem: fixed feasts fall 13 days later on our calendar (Christmas on 7 January, the Annunciation on 7 April, the Holy Cross on 27 September), and Easter follows the Julian rule. Orthodox Churches on the revised calendar, such as those of Greece and Romania, keep the fixed feasts on the Catholic dates.
notes.computed: The dates are calculated, not copied from a parish calendar. Please confirm the times of services with the church.

maryMotherOfGod.name: Mary, Mother of God
maryMotherOfGod.description: The year opens with Mary, the Mother of God, on the eighth day of Christmas.

epiphany.name: Epiphany
epiphany.description: Christ is revealed to the world: the Magi in the West, his Baptism in the Jordan in the East.

presentation.name: Presentation of the Lord
presentation.description: Mary and Joseph bring the Child Jesus to the Temple, where Simeon and Anna meet him.

cleanMonday.name: Clean Monday
cleanMonday.description: The first day of Great Lent in the Orthodox Church.

ashWednesday.name: Ash Wednesday
ashWednesday.description: Lent begins: forty days of prayer, fasting and charity before Easter.

stJoseph.name: Saint Joseph
stJoseph.description: Joseph of Nazareth, husband of Mary and guardian of Jesus.

annunciation.name: Annunciation of the Lord
annunciation.description: The angel Gabriel greets Mary here in Nazareth: the feast of the city’s two churches of the Annunciation.

palmSunday.name: Palm Sunday
palmSunday.orthodoxName: Entry of the Lord into Jerusalem
palmSunday.description: Jesus enters Jerusalem and Holy Week begins.

holyThursday.name: Holy Thursday
holyThursday.description: The Last Supper: Jesus gives the Eucharist and washes the feet of his disciples.

goodFriday.name: Good Friday
goodFriday.description: The Passion and death of Jesus on the Cross.

holySaturday.name: Holy Saturday
holySaturday.description: The Church keeps watch at the tomb until the first light of Easter.

easter.name: Easter Sunday
easter.description: The Resurrection of the Lord, the feast of feasts.

divineMercy.name: Divine Mercy Sunday
divineMercy.description: The Second Sunday of Easter, dedicated to the mercy of God.

ascension.name: Ascension of the Lord
ascension.description: Forty days after Easter, Jesus is taken up into heaven.

pentecost.name: Pentecost
pentecost.description: The Holy Spirit comes down on the apostles, fifty days after Easter.

trinity.name: Trinity Sunday
trinity.description: The Sunday after Pentecost, in honour of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

corpusChristi.name: Corpus Christi
corpusChristi.description: The Body and Blood of Christ, honoured in the Eucharist and in processions.

transfiguration.name: Transfiguration of the Lord
transfiguration.description: Jesus shines in glory on Mount Tabor, a few kilometres from Nazareth.

assumption.name: Assumption of Mary
assumption.description: Mary is taken up into the glory of heaven; the East calls it her falling asleep.

nativityOfMary.name: Nativity of Mary
nativityOfMary.description: The birthday of the Virgin Mary.

holyCross.name: Exaltation of the Holy Cross
holyCross.description: The feast of the Cross of Christ, which gives Nazareth Holy Cross its name.

allSaints.name: All Saints
allSaints.description: All the saints of God, known and unknown, in one feast.

advent1.name: First Sunday of Advent
advent1.description: The Church’s new year begins with four weeks of waiting for Christmas.

advent2.name: Second Sunday of Advent
advent2.description: Advent: prepare the way of the Lord.

advent3.name: Third Sunday of Advent
advent3.description: Gaudete Sunday: rejoice, the Lord is near.

advent4.name: Fourth Sunday of Advent
advent4.description: The last Sunday before Christmas, with Mary who awaits her Son.

immaculateConception.name: Immaculate Conception
immaculateConception.description: Mary, kept free from all sin from the first moment of her life.

christmas.name: Christmas
christmas.description: The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem.

activities.title: Things to do
activities.lead: A few ways to spend your days in the city, beyond its churches.

oldcity.title: Walk the Old City and its market
oldcity.text: Narrow lanes, arched passages and the old market, where spices, sweets and crafts are sold side by side.

basilica.title: Pray in the Basilica of the Annunciation
basilica.text: Sit in silence in the grotto where tradition places the Annunciation, or join a Mass in the upper church.

trail.title: Walk a stretch of the Jesus Trail
trail.text: The trail begins in Nazareth and crosses the hills of Galilee towards the Sea of Galilee. Its first kilometres already open wide views.

precipice.title: Watch the sunset from Mount Precipice
precipice.text: From the cliff above the Jezreel Valley the whole plain lies below you, golden at the end of the day.

food.title: Taste Nazareth
food.text: The city is known for its sweets and its home cooking: try knafeh, served warm.

christmas.title: Christmas in Nazareth
christmas.text: In December the city lights up, with a Christmas market and a festive parade on Christmas Eve.

plan.title: Plan your days in Nazareth
plan.lead: Choose how many days you have and what you love: the pilgrim planner draws a route with walking times. The visitor guide has the seasons, the ways here and practical advice.
